newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: FOREIGN AFFAIRS SAYS NOT AWARE OF ASSASSSINATION ATTEMPT
The Foreign affairs Department says it's not aware of any evidence of a plot to kill East Timorese Nobel Prize winner, Carlos Belo.
The Auxilliary Catholic Bishop for Melbourne, Hilton Deakin, says he's been told an Indonesian soldier was paid to kill Bishop Belo on Christmas Eve.
Bishop Deakin, says he's been told the soldier was himself killed by the crowd at the bishop's homecoming from the Nobel Prize presenttion.
A Foreign Affairs Spokesman says the Department's aware of the report that a person was killed who had been attempting to assassinate Bishop Belo.
He says the Department understands the situation was very tense on Christmas eve, with tens of thousands of people waiting to greet the Bishop.
LIFE BANS POSSIBLE FORE SYDNEY SPORTS HOOLIGANS
Sydney's two major sporting venues now have the power to ban sports hooligans for life.
As of today, the Sydney Cricket Ground and the Sydney Football Stadium can impose bans on those found guilty of pitch invasion or offensive behaviour.
Under the New South Wales government's crackdown on sports hooligans, field invaders will face a 12 month ban from sporting events held at either venue.
If they breach the 12 month ban, they'll be charged with trespass and banned for life.
The bans follow unruly behaviour at the SCG this season, such as on New Year's Day when eight people were arrested for running onto the field, and 85 others were ejected from the ground.
NSW Minister for sport and recreation, Gabrielle Harrison, says financial penalties for the offences will also be introduced in the future.
ARRESTS AT LOGGING PROTEST IN VICTORIA
Police have arrested three people who locked themselves to a bulldozer in an anti-logging protest on the edge of the Errinundra National Park in Victoria's East Gippsland region.
About 35 people began protesting early this morning against further ring-barking of the national park.
Most avoided arrest.
CAPOBIANCO NOT CONFIDENT ABOUT HEARING

Western Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco is not confident of clearing his name over drug-taking allegations at next month's hearing of the International Amateur Athletics Federation in Monte Carlo.
Capobianco tested positive at a meeting in Europe before the Atlanta Olympics.
He was allowed to run in Atlanta after successfully contesting the finding in the court of sport arbitration.
The IAAF is now challenging that decision and Capobianco faces a mandatory four-year ban if he loses his case.
He says fighting the allegations has so far cost him a quarter of a million dollars and the hearing will be tough.
LATEST FROM THE AUSTRALIAN OPEN
Mark Woodforde and Scott Draper are the only Aussies left in the singles draw of the Australian Open, after the elimination of Todd Woodbridge today.
Woodbridge took the first set against Malivai Washington, but the American dominated the rest of the match, winning 4-6, 6-2, 6-3, 6-1.
Meanwhile, women's top seed, Steffi Graf, has overcome a nearly disastrous start, to win her third round match, against Argentina's Ines Borrochategui.
At one stage, Borrochategui was up 5-2, and serving for the first set, but was unable to see it through, and Graf came back to win 7-5, 6-3.
Others to win through today include Anke Huber, Lindsay Davenport, and Andrei Medvedev.
And, former women's champion, Mary Pierce has won her match against Marketa Kochta, 6-0, 6-2.
BHP INDUSTRIAL HEARING CONTINUES

A dispute that's stalled construction of BHP's one-point-five billion dollar iron plant in Port Hedland is about to return to the Industrial Relations Commission in Perth. More than 600 construction workers have been on strike for more than a fortnight in the dispute over pay and conditions.
On Wednesday, they rejected a Commission recommendation to return to work.
The workers are seeking wage rises up to 38 per cent above award rates, and a living away from home allowance of 500 dollars a week.
SIX YEARS JAIL FOR SEX WITH DAUGHTER
In the District Court in Perth, a 43-year-old man has been sentenced to six years jail for sexually interfering with his daughter.
The court was told the offences occurred between January 1993, when the girl was aged 10, and September 1996 at the family home.
Chief Judge, Kevin Hammond, said the issue of whether the girl consented to the activity was irrelevant.
He said an eight year prison term would be appropriate, but deducted two years because the man pleaded guilty at the first opportunity.
The man will be eligible for parole.
Today's sentence follows controversy over the sentencing of another sex offender by District Court Judge Nigel Clark.
Judge Clark caused an uprooar by saying that in some instances, sexual abuse could be pleasurable and not necessarily harmful to the victims.
The offender in that case, who'd had a sexual relationship with his teenage daughter, received a two year suspended sentence.
However the case is the subject of an appeal by the Director of Public Prosecutions.
NSW SAYS IT'S NO RACE ON EVENT LINEUP
New South Wales denies it's missing out on major sporting events...and the associated tourism spinoffs...at the hands of Victoria.
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr, after today announcing Sydney will be a port of call for the Whitbread Round the World Yacht Race, says there's no race between the two states.
Mr Carr says Sydney has 70 percent of the tourist dollar spent in Australia...and justly won the Whitbread over Melbourne, which had actively sought the port of call.
Yesterday Victoria was successful in stealing the national athletics championships away from Sydney.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
